subject: A Level Chemistry
title: Energy profile with a catalyst
question:
Fig. 4.1 shows the energy profile for an exothermic reaction, with and without a catalyst.
(a) State what is meant by the term activation energy.
(b) Use Fig. 4.1 to explain how a catalyst increases the rate of reaction.
(c) State the sign of ΔH for this reaction and explain your answer.

scene: First try: the smooth curve dipped below the reactant level before rising and bumped up again near the products, which is wrong for an energy profile.
Second try: the renderer now has a curve option for graphs that never overshoots its points.
tikz: The curves are drawn with hand placed control points, so they cannot overshoot.

figure:
An energy profile diagram. The vertical axis is labelled energy and the horizontal axis progress of reaction, with no numbers.
The reactants start on a flat level. The curve rises to a single peak and falls to a flat products level, lower than the reactants because the reaction is exothermic.
A solid curve without a catalyst, and a dashed curve with a catalyst that has a lower peak. Both start and end at the same levels.
A double headed arrow from the reactant level to the top of the uncatalysed peak, labelled Ea. An arrow from the reactant level down to the product level, labelled ΔH.
Label: reactants, products, with catalyst, without catalyst.
Caption: Fig. 4.1.
